title: The control-room lane can drive a goal to a CONTRACT-BOUND, criterion-VERIFIED, LANDED state
description:
PREREQUISITE filed by worker-ca28be90 on 2026-09-07 from task-817d893fa1254a4d82d2888af1f87a47 (the Gate 3 Release proof row), whose DoD-5 is unsatisfiable without this. Measurement in that row's comment-196f88ab (probe output), comment-98ba58b4 (probe source) and comment-6023f9fb (gap, symbol by symbol). Global rail 4 clause 2: the capability is absent, so this is a prerequisite production row rather than a narrowed DoD or a mock-backed journey.

THE GAP, MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) BY RUNNING THE LANE, NOT BY READING IT.
The control-room Playwright lane (`tests/e2e/control-room/daemon-ports.ts`) seeds with the SHIPPED demo seed. That seed produces a LEGACY Foundation goal. Probe output, verbatim:

  GRAPHS    [{"goalRef":"goal-live-1","run":"run-live-1"}]
  BINDING   goal-live-1 {"ok":false,"code":"COMPILED_CONTRACT_BINDING_ABSENT"}
  CRITERION goal-live-1 {"ok":false,"code":"COMPILED_CONTRACT_BINDING_ABSENT","layer":"CRITERION_EVIDENCE"}
  DOSSIER   goal-live-1 NULL

`demo-seed-payloads.ts` drives `planning.create_draft`/`ready`/`claim`/`finalize_submission` (:143,:150,:161,:209) and has ZERO `product_contract` hits, so it never reaches `runSubmitDecomposition`, which is the only place `compile-dispatcher.ts:290` mints the binding. `goal-approved-execution-scope.ts:31-42` documents this goal shape by name: "The existing Foundation leg has no Product Contract binding". This is by construction and permanent, not a bug.

CONSEQUENCE FOR EVERY CONSUMER, not just the release row: any browser journey needing `/release/read` PRESENT, criterion coverage, `goal.close`'s contract gate, or a dossier is inert on this lane. `goal-release.tsx:90` gates its control on `sha !== null`, so the card renders honest and DISABLED - the dispatch is unreachable from the browser, so even a REFUSED-path journey cannot be written.

WHAT EXISTS AND CAN BE COMPOSED. `tests/e2e/foundation/multi-node-journey.ts:1-17` already drives the exact chain: goal.create_with_source -> product_contract.propose_revision -> product_contract.approve_gate_1 -> planning.submit_decomposition (daemon compiles, seals, MINTS THE BINDING) -> approval.decide_intent; `multi-node-criteria.ts` drives criterion approval plus checks. `multi-node-wire.ts` `daemonWire(origin, operatorCredential)` already takes an arbitrary origin.

WHY IT IS NOT AN IMPORT. Identities are MODULE CONSTANTS bound to the foundation scratch, not parameters: `multi-node-graph-harness.ts:47-66` fixes GOAL_ID, PROJECT_ID="moe-e2e-multi-node", CONTRACT_ID, REVISION_ID, OPERATOR_CREDENTIAL, AGENT_SESSION/HUMAN_SESSION and node keys ALPHA/BETA/OMEGA; `multi-node-wire.ts` fixes CSRF_TOKEN. The control-room lane runs MOE_PROJECT_ID=e2e-proj-<tag>, csrf `e2e-daemon-lane-csrf`, credential `e2e-daemon-lane-credential`, node ref `node-e2e-<tag>` (daemon-ports.ts:70-71,132-155,311), and `createLaneScratch` writes exactly ONE node spec by design.

THE SHAPE OF THE WORK: parameterise the five foundation modules on project/credential/csrf/goal/node identity WITHOUT changing what `tests/e2e/foundation/multi-node-graph.e2e.test.ts` proves (that suite must stay green with its current constants as defaults), then expose ONE control-room helper - a sibling of `lane-landing.ts` - that takes a `DaemonLane` and returns a goal that is contract-bound, criterion-verified and landed. Do NOT hand-seed a criterion graph and do NOT weaken any consumer assertion; a helper that writes store rows directly is fabricated authority and defeats the point.
definitionOfDone: One exported control-room lane helper (a sibling of tests/e2e/control-room/lane-landing.ts) takes a DaemonLane and returns a goal whose readCriterionGoal is ok, whose readReleaseDossierInput is non-null, and whose criteria carry no gaps - every byte of it driven through the daemon's REAL command edges (product_contract.propose_revision, product_contract.approve_gate_1, planning.submit_decomposition, approval.decide_intent, the criterion approval/check chain). Assert the readers' ok/non-null results from the helper's own arm; a store row written directly by the helper is fabricated authority and rejects the row.

The five foundation modules (multi-node-graph-harness.ts, multi-node-journey.ts, multi-node-world.ts, multi-node-wire.ts, multi-node-criteria.ts) are parameterised on project id, operator credential, csrf token, goal id and node identity, with their CURRENT constants as defaults. Proof: `pnpm test:e2e` runs green with its count line quoted and tests/e2e/foundation/multi-node-graph.e2e.test.ts named in the output - unchanged behaviour, not merely unchanged source.

The lane can LAND on the contract-bound goal: the helper composes with landLaneNode (or states in its own comment exactly why it cannot and what it does instead), and a real sha is asserted with /^[0-9a-f]{40}$/. A goal that is contract-bound but unlandable satisfies nothing downstream, because release.decide is gated on the landed commit (affordance-planning-offers.ts:293).

A committed arm proves the negative that motivated this row: on the SHIPPED-seed lane readCriterionGoal refuses exactly COMPILED_CONTRACT_BINDING_ABSENT at layer CRITERION_EVIDENCE, and on the helper's goal it is ok. Assert the refusal CODE and its LAYER, not merely that one failed and one did not (global rail 1).

Gates quoted with count lines, each run standalone and foreground: `pnpm test:e2e` (names the multi-node spec), `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`, and `pnpm test:e2e:browser` under the browser-e2e-gate lease with its SPEC COUNT quoted. An exit-0 leg with no count line ran nothing (global rail 8).
taskRails: DO NOT HAND-SEED. Every durable fact this helper produces is driven through a shipped command kind over the daemon's real HTTP edge. A helper that writes store rows or synthesises a binding is fabricated authority and defeats every consumer that depends on it.

THE FOUNDATION SUITE MUST STAY GREEN AND MUST STAY AS STRONG. Parameterising is a defaults-preserving refactor; if a foundation assertion has to weaken to make a constant a parameter, stop and split instead.
PARAMETERISE, DO NOT FORK. A copied multi-node harness under tests/e2e/control-room/ is a second authority that will drift from the one the foundation suite proves.

The helper RETURNS the goal, and its own arm asserts the three things DoD 1 names, read through the production readers: `readCriterionGoal` is ok, `readReleaseDossierInput` is non-null, and the criteria carry no gaps. SPLIT AT PLAN TIME, plus two corrections to the filed shape. Measured at HEAD, 2026-09-07.

1. SPLIT. DoD 2 (parameterise the foundation modules) is now leaf row **task-371677fc977948a597fa9b821b99f939**, filed in PLANNING; this row's `dependsOn` names it and WORKING claims are gated until it is DONE. The remaining clauses (the lane helper, the landing, the negative arm, the gates) stay here.

WHY, not as paperwork: the parameterisation is a defaults-preserving refactor whose whole proof is the foundation suite staying green, and it has zero dependency on the control-room lane. The helper needs three module directories, three wrapper passes with real seats, an in-process criterion service and a landing, on a lane whose scratch writes exactly ONE node spec. BOTH halves gate on ~15-minute journeys (`JOURNEY_TIMEOUT_MS = 900_000` in multi-node-graph.e2e.test.ts), so landing them together makes one long red indistinguishable from the other. Rail: name every consumer at plan time, and a split that would otherwise be discovered at step 5 is a plan-time split.

2. CORRECTION — THE ROW SAYS FIVE MODULES; `multi-node-reads.ts` IS NOT ONE OF THEM AND NEEDS NO WORK. `grep -n "GOAL_ID\|PROJECT_ID\|MULTI_NODE_KEYS\|CRITERIA" tests/e2e/foundation/multi-node-reads.ts` returns ZERO hits — it already takes identity as arguments. Related: `multi-node-wire.ts:23` does not define the csrf token, it IMPORTS `CSRF_TOKEN` from `j1-loop-harness.js`, which many unrelated journeys share — so the parameter defaults to that import and `j1-loop-harness.ts` is never edited. Both facts are recorded on the leaf row's description and rails.

3. A SIXTH PARAMETER DIMENSION NOBODY NAMED, and it is why this row cannot start first. `sealMultiNodeGraph` opens with `for (const planned of worldPrelude(scratch, clock)) await send(wire, planned)`, and `worldPrelude` (multi-node-world.ts:46-71) replays the shipped seed's prelude **through `project.activate`**. The control-room lane has ALREADY run the shipped demo seed and activated its project. Sealing on the lane therefore needs the prelude SKIPPED, not merely re-identified. That is a change to the foundation modules, so it is a DoD clause on the leaf, not something this row can work around.

4. THE LANE ENVIRONMENT NEEDS NO SHARED-FILE EDIT. `wrapperEnv` (wrapper-lane.ts:131) returns a plain frozen record, so the helper spreads it and adds the three keys the foundation run sets — `MOE_NODE_SPECS_DIR: ""` (so only COMPILED nodes are staffed; the lane's single operator spec is irrelevant because compiled missions come from the sealed graph), `MOE_NODE_TEST_COMMAND`, `MOE_NODE_WORKSPACE`. `daemon-ports.ts` and `wrapper-lane.ts` are task-cf2d91d9's declared paths and this plan edits NEITHER.

5. THREE WRAPPER PASSES, NOT ONE. The lane sets `MOE_WRAPPER_MAX_AGENTS: "1"`, and ALPHA/BETA are independent while OMEGA depends on both — the same 2-producer-passes-plus-1-consumer-pass shape `multi-node-graph.e2e.test.ts` drives. The plan asserts OMEGA stayed undelivered until its producers landed, because an assertion that only checks the final state cannot distinguish a working dependency gate from a broken one.

6. NO SHORTCUT TO "criterion-verified" EXISTS. `approveAndRunCriteria` refuses unless `ready.integratedArtifact !== null`, which only exists once nodes are delivered and landed. Anything lighter is hand-seeding, which this row's own rails forbid. Confirmed rather than assumed, so nobody re-litigates it mid-flight.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD, 2026-09-07, BY READING THE MODULES — the description's probe output is confirmed and its module claims are accurate except one, corrected below.

THE DESCRIPTION IS RIGHT ABOUT THE GAP. The lane seeds with the shipped demo seed, which drives `planning.create_draft`/`ready`/`claim`/`finalize_submission` and never reaches `runSubmitDecomposition`, the only place `compile-dispatcher.ts:290` mints the binding. So `readCriterionGoal` refuses `COMPILED_CONTRACT_BINDING_ABSENT` at layer `CRITERION_EVIDENCE` on the lane's `goal-live-1`. Both readers exist and are importable from an e2e spec: `readCriterionGoal` (apps/daemon/src/criterion-evidence/criterion-goal.ts:19) and `readReleaseDossierInput` (apps/daemon/src/release/release-durable-facts.ts:89). The TS6059 fear about importing apps/daemon from this directory is stale — `design-operator.spec.ts` already does it.

ONE CORRECTION TO THE FILED SHAPE: the row says "the five foundation modules", and `multi-node-reads.ts` (265 lines) is NOT among them and does NOT need parameterising — `grep -n "GOAL_ID\|PROJECT_ID\|MULTI_NODE_KEYS\|CRITERIA"` on it returns ZERO hits; it already takes identity as arguments. Also `multi-node-wire.ts:23` imports `CSRF_TOKEN` from `j1-loop-harness.js` rather than defining it, so the csrf parameter defaults to that import and `j1-loop-harness.ts` (shared by many unrelated journeys) is never edited. Both facts are recorded on the leaf row.

THE SIXTH DIMENSION NOBODY NAMED, and the reason this row cannot start before the leaf lands: `sealMultiNodeGraph` opens with `for (const planned of worldPrelude(scratch, clock)) await send(wire, planned)`, and `worldPrelude` (multi-node-world.ts:46-71) replays the shipped seed's prelude THROUGH `project.activate`. The control-room lane has ALREADY run the shipped demo seed and activated its project. Sealing a graph on the lane therefore needs the prelude SKIPPED, not merely re-identified — which is why the leaf row carries a DoD clause for it.

WHAT THE HELPER MUST DRIVE, read off `multi-node-graph.e2e.test.ts`: seal (HTTP) -> `MULTI_NODE_KEYS` = three nodes, ALPHA and BETA independent and OMEGA depending on both -> THREE wrapper passes, because `MOE_WRAPPER_MAX_AGENTS` is "1" on the lane and one seat delivers one node per pass -> `approveAndRunCriteria` (three approvals, one verify offer, then an in-process `createCriterionEvidenceService().advance()`) -> `closeCompletedGoal`. planningNotes.risks:
THIS ROW CANNOT START UNTIL task-371677fc IS DONE. Its `dependsOn` enforces that. The prelude-skip and the identity parameters are that row's deliverables; a worker who finds them missing must NOT re-implement them here — that would fork the harness, which this row's own rail forbids.

PROCESS LEAKS ARE THE REAL FAILURE MODE, and there are now more children than any previous lane row: the lane's daemon and dev server, up to three wrapper runs, the seats each spawns, and the landing wrapper. Every one must join the caller's `tracked` list and be killed in a `finally` on EVERY exit path including the refusing ones — copy `landLaneNode`'s shape exactly.
